content.text:
Rename the real-tool suite in PR #639 (branch wp-verify-real-in-ci; check it out in a worktree, push to the same branch). Trail #460. The name verify-real says nothing; it runs Callisto against the real npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, uv and Changesets tools and local real registries. Rename the just recipes verify-real -> test-real-tools and verify-real-tools -> install-real-tools, the CI job to 'Real Tool Tests', and the install action if its name says verify-real. Update every reference: justfile, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING, docs, .github workflows and actions, test file comments, target/verify-real -> target/real-tools. Don't rename the test file unless a reference requires it. git grep -n 'verify-real' must return nothing afterwards. Run just workflow-contracts and just doc-check. Merge origin/main, push. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be fast and lean; GitHub CI runs the full suite, so don't duplicate it.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Local checks: `cargo test -p <touched crate>` and `just lint` (clippy) for the crates you touched; `just doc-check` if docs changed. Do not run local `just ci` or a fresh reviewer unless the lead asks; let GitHub CI do the full run.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.

docs/architecture/release.md:153:`just verify-real` rehearses recovery against local registries through the production registry binding, with no test-only allowance in the https rule: Verdaccio, `pypiserver` and a JSON simple index serve a self-signed loopback certificate that npm, curl and Twine trust through their own CA variables. The rehearsals are a partial npm publish adopted by a rerun, a PyPI index that shows an upload late or never, a remote tag on another commit, and a PyPI release whose index lacks one built file. Cargo is rehearsed through a `kind = "cargo"` registry named in `publish-to`: a local sparse registry with the publish and download API stands behind `[registries.<name>] index` in a scratch `CARGO_HOME`, and callisto passes `--registry <name>` to `cargo publish` and `cargo info`. The Cargo registry is plain `http` on loopback because callisto never sees its URL, so no https rule applies to it. The Cargo rehearsals are a partial publish adopted by a rerun, an index that shows a publish late (cargo itself does not wait), and a remote tag on another commit. A `crates-io` publish runs plain `cargo publish`, so it is not rehearsed against a local registry.
docs/architecture/release.md:155:`just verify-real` also runs the real `@changesets/cli` 3.x and 2.x beside callisto in scratch npm workspaces and compares versions. One scenario plans a fixed group in Changesets, runs `callisto init`, and expects the same packages and versions from `callisto version --dry-run`; the other enters a pre cycle with Changesets, then expects callisto to give the next beta and the exit release Changesets itself gives. `init` does not translate `fixed`, so the first scenario adds the `[[fixed-group]]` the `init` warning names. Changesets 3.x `init` asks questions on a TTY, so only 2.x runs it; 3.x gets its default config written.
docs/architecture/release.md:157:`just verify-real` then runs `native_resolution_e2e_tests` and fails when `npm`, `pnpm` or `uv` is missing, so the matrix is recorded rather than skipped. After `version` or `snapshot` each ecosystem's own locked install must still succeed:
